title: Core: Fix `react-docgen-typescript` support in story creation
body:
## What I did This reintroduces support for `react-docgen-typescript` and its options defined in `main.ts`, which were supported before and therefore this fixes that issue. ## Checklist for Contributors ### Testing #### The changes in this PR are covered in the following automated tests: - [ ] stories - [x] unit tests - [ ] integration tests - [ ] end-to-end tests #### Manual testing 1. Define react-docgen-typescript usage in main.ts like so: ```ts const config = defineMain({ typescript: { reactDocgen: 'react-docgen-typescript', }, }); export default config; ``` 2. Run Storybook and create a story for a typescript heavy component like ```tsx // ERROR: React docgen doesn't identify anything from MediumTitle import { ComponentProps, FC, PropsWithChildren } from 'react'; type Sizes = 'large' | 'medium' | 'small'; const Title: FC> = ({ color, size = 'large', children, }) => (
{children}
); export const MediumTitle: FC, 'size'>> = (props) => ( ); ``` 3. See args being created correctly 4. Switch back to `react-docgen` in main.ts 5. Delete the previously generated story file and do the same flow for the same component 6. See that the flow is faster but less precise on args <!-- Please include the steps to test your changes here. For example: 1. Run a sandbox for template, e.g. `yarn task --task sandbox --start-from auto --template react-vite/default-ts` 3. Open Storybook in your browser 8. _⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟡 Minor_

**Mock placement issue: `vi.mock` is called inside a test case.**

Per coding guidelines, mocks should be placed at the top of the test file before any test cases, not inside individual tests. Additionally, `vi.mock` is hoisted by Vitest, so calling it inside a test doesn't work as expected - the mock applies to the entire module.


<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

Move the mock to the top of the file and configure behavior in `beforeEach`:

```diff
+vi.mock('react-docgen-typescript', { spy: true });
+
+// At module top, after imports
+
 describe('extractArgTypesFromDocgenTypescript', () => {
+  beforeEach(() => {
+    vi.spyOn(process, 'cwd').mockReturnValue('/app');
+    vol.fromJSON(fsMocks, '/app');
+    
+    // Configure mock behavior here
+  });
+
   test('extracts arg types from a simple component', async () => {
-    // ...
-    vi.mock('react-docgen-typescript', () => ({
-      withCompilerOptions: vi.fn().mockReturnValue(mockParser),
-    }));
```
</details>

As per coding guidelines, mocks should use `vi.mock()` with the `spy: true` option and mock implementations should be in `beforeEach` blocks.

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
In
`@code/renderers/react/src/componentManifest/reactDocgen/extractReactTypescriptDocgenInfo.test.ts`
around lines 188 - 191, The vi.mock call that stubs 'react-docgen-typescript' is
currently inside a test and must be moved to the top of the test file so it is
hoisted correctly; change the module mock invocation to
vi.mock('react-docgen-typescript', { spy: true, }, ) at file top (outside tests)
and remove the in-test vi.mock; then configure mock behavior (e.g. make
withCompilerOptions return mockParser) inside a beforeEach block by setting the
mock implementation/returnValue on the mocked withCompilerOptions function
(referencing withCompilerOptions and mockParser) so each test gets a fresh,
configured mock.
```

</details>

🌐 Web query:

`react-docgen v8 PropDescriptor tsType type fields structure`

💡 Result:

Short answer — in react-docgen v8 a prop's tsType is a TypeDescriptor<TSFunctionSignatureType>, which is a tagged union. The possible shapes and their important fields are:

- TSFunctionSignatureType (function signature)
  - signature: { arguments: Array<FunctionArgumentType>, return?: TypeDescriptor, this?: TypeDescriptor }.
  - each FunctionArgumentType: { name: string; rest?: boolean; type?: TypeDescriptor }.[1]

- ObjectSignatureType (object / interface)
  - properties: Array<{ key: TypeDescriptor | string; value: TypeDescriptor; description?: string }>.
  - constructor?: TypeDescriptor.[1]

- ElementsType (array/tuple of element types)
  - elements: Array<TypeDescriptor>; name: 'elements' (type kind).[1]

- LiteralType
  - raw, value (literal details) — represents literal types (e.g. "foo", 1). [1][2]

- SimpleType
  - name: string; raw?: string — basic named types (e.g. 'string', 'number', 'union', etc.).[1][2]

Notes:
- TypeDescriptor<T> is defined as ElementsType | LiteralType | ObjectSignatureType<T> | SimpleType | T (so a tsType may itself be a TS function-signature node).  
- Use the getTSType / getTypeAnnotation utilities to see how these are produced. [1][2]

Sources: react-docgen v8 type definitions. [1] API/index (dist .d.ts) and [2] package main type exports.

**Add fallback to support props with only the `type` field.**

The `PropDescriptor` has both `tsType` and `type` fields. The current code only checks `tsType`, causing props with only a `type` field to be dropped. This can happen with JavaScript/PropTypes components. Add a fallback to the `type` field:

<details>
<summary>🔧 Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
   for (const [propName, propInfo] of Object.entries(props)) {
     const tsType = (propInfo as ReactDocgenPropDescriptor).tsType as ReactDocgenTsType | undefined;
-    if (!tsType) {
+    const fallbackType = (propInfo as ReactDocgenPropDescriptor).type as ReactDocgenTsType | undefined;
+    const docgenType = tsType ?? fallbackType;
+    if (!docgenType) {
       continue;
     }
     mapped.props![propName] = {
       required: Boolean((propInfo as ReactDocgenPropDescriptor).required),
-      type: mapReactDocgenToArgType(tsType),
+      type: mapReactDocgenToArgType(docgenType),
     };
   }
```
</details>

<!-- suggestion_start -->

<details>
<summary>📝 Committable suggestion</summary>

> ‼️ **IMPORTANT**
> Carefully review the code before committing. Ensure that it accurately replaces the highlighted code, contains no missing lines, and has no issues with indentation. Thoroughly test & benchmark the code to ensure it meets the requirements.

```suggestion
  for (const [propName, propInfo] of Object.entries(props)) {
    const tsType = (propInfo as ReactDocgenPropDescriptor).tsType as ReactDocgenTsType | undefined;
    const fallbackType = (propInfo as ReactDocgenPropDescriptor).type as ReactDocgenTsType | undefined;
    const docgenType = tsType ?? fallbackType;
    if (!docgenType) {
      continue;
    }
    mapped.props![propName] = {
      required: Boolean((propInfo as ReactDocgenPropDescriptor).required),
      type: mapReactDocgenToArgType(docgenType),
    };
```

</details>

<!-- suggestion_end -->

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
In
`@code/renderers/react/src/componentManifest/reactDocgen/extractReactDocgenInfo.ts`
around lines 150 - 158, The loop in extractReactDocgenInfo.ts currently ignores
props that lack tsType; update the logic in the for-loop that iterates over
props (where tsType is derived from (propInfo as
ReactDocgenPropDescriptor).tsType) to fall back to (propInfo as
ReactDocgenPropDescriptor).type when tsType is undefined, and pass that fallback
into mapReactDocgenToArgType so props defined with PropTypes/type are preserved;
keep setting required via (propInfo as ReactDocgenPropDescriptor).required and
assign the result into mapped.props![propName]. Ensure mapReactDocgenToArgType
can accept the docgen "type" shape or normalize it before mapping.
```

</details>

The matching logic at line 149 uses `d.filePath?.includes(componentExportName)`, which is a substring match. This could incorrectly match components when the export name is a substring of another file path:

const match = docgens.find((d) => {
  if (d.displayName === componentExportName) return true;

    return fileName === componentExportName;

});
